item.title: Algebraic criteria for complete relaxation in autonomous and periodically driven open quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.29084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive sufficient criteria that guarantee convergence of open quantum system dynamics to a unique long-time state independent of the initial conditions. We refer to this behavior as complete relaxation. Focusing on systems described by Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equations on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, our approach uses only elementary mathematical arguments. For autonomous systems, we recover three previously derived relaxation criteria, which can be expressed as algebraic conditions on the Lindblad operators and the Hamiltonian entering the GKSL equation. For periodically driven systems, we obtain a new criterion involving a similar algebraic condition and a local continuity requirement on the time-dependent GKSL generator. This result implies an earlier criterion for complete relaxation formulated in Ref. [J. Phys. A 52, 43LT01 (2019)]. We also discuss implications of our approach for periodically modulated classical master equations, as well as extensions to driven systems without a periodicity constraint.
item.dc:creator: Paul Menczel, Kay Brandner

item.title: Splitting Probability in Monitored Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.29547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a continuous-time quantum walk stroboscopically subjected to projective measurements on two distinct targets with sampling time period $\tau$. We construct a general renewal framework for the first-detection amplitude at each target, from which we obtain the associated splitting probabilities. For Hamiltonians with reflection symmetry, we further show that each dual-target first-detection amplitude can be viewed as an interference effect between a pair of single-target first-detection amplitudes. This formulation yields exact expressions for the splitting probabilities and gives special sampling times at which they undergo pointwise discontinuous jumps due to a form of ergodicity breaking associated with dark states. As an illustrative example, we apply the framework to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice chain with nearest-neighbor hopping, and study the splitting probabilities as functions of the initial position and sampling time. Below a critical sampling time, $0<\tau < \tau_c$ where $\tau_c = 2 \pi / \Delta E$ with $\Delta E$ being the energy bandwidth, the splitting probabilities for large system sizes become equal to $1/2$, independent of the initial position, as long as this position does not coincide with target sites. Above the critical sampling time, $\tau \geq \tau_c$, the splitting probabilities deviate from $1/2$ and develop oscillations as a function of initial position. The wavenumber associated with these oscillations is $Q=2\sin^{-1}(r\tau_c/\tau)$, where $r$ is a positive integer. We also explore the effects of relative phase and spatial separation between different components of a coherent initial state on the splitting probabilities. Finally, we study how a finite number of measurements modifies the splitting probabilities and broadens the resonances at special sampling times.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Singh, Sabine Tornow, David A Kessler, Eli Barkai

item.title: Stochastic resonance in time-delayed bistable active particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate analytically and numerically stochastic resonance in an underdamped active (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck) particle confined in a bistable potential with time-delayed feedback and subjected to an additional (non-thermal) white-noise source. Restricting the analysis to the active-noise-dominated bistable regime, with sufficiently short delay and active-noise correlation times, we develop a perturbative theory that yields analytical expressions for both the escape rate and the spectral power amplification within the framework of linear-response theory, without invoking detailed balance. The analytical predictions are in qualitative agreement with direct numerical simulations throughout the perturbative regime. We show that a moderate increase in the active-noise correlation time can enhance the stochastic-resonance response, in marked contrast to previous results for overdamped passive systems driven by colored noise. Conversely, the addition of white noise weakens the resonant response and shifts its optimum toward lower active-noise intensities. Time-delayed feedback further alters the matching condition between the escape rate and the driving frequency while preserving the resonant mechanism. Beyond the perturbative regime, we find that finite-memory effects progressively broaden the resonance profile and substantially decrease its amplitude. Overall, these results provide new insight into the combined role of inertia, activity, environmental fluctuations, and time delayed feedback in stochastic resonance in nonequilibrium systems.
item.dc:creator: Antonio A. Valido, Mattia Coccolo, Miguel A. F. Sanju\'an

item.title: Energy-fed commitment: a minimal model of random selection followed by reinforcement
item.description: arXiv:2610.29670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a symmetric instability is crossed, fluctuations choose one of several equivalent branches. We study a minimal stochastic model of what can then make that choice progressively harder to undo. After selection, the stiffness of the selected state grows in proportion to the energy released each time the structure recovers from a perturbation; in this conservative model that energy equals, up to small and explicitly computed terms, the work absorbed from the perturbing agent. The model is a phenomenological closure with one coupling constant. That energy reinforces a branch already chosen, rather than choosing it, is an assumption of the model, which we state and do not derive. Its consequences are quantitative. The growth of commitment depends on how the structure is driven: geometric under displacement control, linear under energy control and sublinear under force control, so that committed states absorb more work per cycle under displacement control and less under force control. Reinforcement suppresses reversal exponentially; beyond a finite commitment the alternative minimum disappears and reversals become rare crossings of an irreversibility threshold. With unbounded reinforcement a choice is retained forever with positive probability under stated conditions; with saturating reinforcement retention is finite, with a lifetime that grows exponentially with the saturation level. Exact first-passage calculations agree with stochastic simulations; these verify the closure and its analysis but cannot test the physical postulate. We identify the experiments that could: protocols that separate absorbed energy from the number of perturbations, and driven steady states with nonzero housekeeping heat, in which heat and absorbed work differ.
item.dc:creator: Haidar Issa Abbas

item.title: Morphological instability and negative geometric friction from contact with active and driven particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Overdamped particles on a deformable substrate induce a geometric friction through their response to metric perturbations. Nonequilibrium dynamics couples such a perturbation to kinetic effects, which can flip that friction negative, softening the substrate's rigidity and favoring invaginations and evaginations. A breathing circle, with local curvature radius as dynamical variable, is the main example. At equilibrium the friction reduces to an ordinary potential response and stays positive. Geometric response emerges as a new route by which active and driven matter reshape their environment.
item.dc:creator: Forouh Maleki, Christian Maes

item.title: Stockmayer Fluid with a Shifted Dipole. III. Ion Solvation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Though ion solvation is well understood for the standard Stockmayer fluid, the effect of displacing the point dipole of a Stockmayer particle, a simple geometric modification, on ion-solvent structuring and solvation thermodynamics remains less understood. We use molecular dynamics simulations to describe how a dipole shift affects radial and orientational solvent structure around centered ions, how strongly the solvent distinguishes cations and anions, and how the solvent mediates ion-ion pairing. We show that, with a centered dipole, cations and anions have equal preferences for the local solvent environment. Shifting the dipole breaks the fore-aft symmetry of the local electrostatic field, leading to a stronger preference for a Stockmayer particle's dipole to orient towards an anion and a weaker preference to orient away from a cation. These structural asymmetries propagate to the solvation free energies: increasing dipole displacement makes anion solvation more favorable, while cation solvation becomes less favorable overall across dipole strengths. The same asymmetry also manifests in the effective ion-ion interaction-increasing the dipole shift reorganizes the local solvation environment, enhancing solvent shielding of short-range cation-anion contact while weakening screening at longer range. As a result, solvent-separated configurations become comparatively more favorable, whereas increasing dipole strength produces the opposite trend. Such effects cannot be explained by bulk dielectric screening alone, indicating that molecular charge geometry plays an important role in both single-ion solvation and solvent-mediated ion-ion interactions. This work demonstrates that dipole location, not only magnitude, provides a geometric control on ion-specific solvation and ion pairing in general polar fluids.
item.dc:creator: Ananya Venkatachalam, Pierre J. Walker, Samuel Varner, Bilin Zhuang, Zhen-Gang Wang

item.title: Microscopic Parametric Correlations and Spectral Rigidity in the Non-Hermitian Threefold Way
item.description: arXiv:2609.13434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study microscopic spectral correlations between two nearby parameter values in the three non-Hermitian Gaussian bulk classes: $A$ (unconstrained), $AI^\dagger$ (complex symmetric), and $AII^\dagger$ (complex self-dual, with each degenerate doublet counted once). Parameter dependence is modelled by stationary matrix Ornstein--Uhlenbeck evolution, whose microscopic time scale is $N^{-1}$. For every positive integer replica number $n$, we derive exact finite-$N$ auxiliary-field integral representations for joint characteristic-polynomial moments and obtain their bulk asymptotics as $N\to\infty$ with $n$ fixed. With the spectrum normalized to the unit disk, correlations near a bulk point $z_0$, between spectral positions $z_1,z_2$ at times $t_1,t_2$, depend only on $s=N|z_1-z_2|^2+N(1-|z_0|^2)|t_1-t_2|$. Adopting the static Hermitian/non-Hermitian replica continuation yields explicit two-time kernels; for $AI^\dagger$ and $AII^\dagger$ these are replica conjectures and, to our knowledge, the first microscopic two-time kernels proposed for these classes. They determine density correlations, cross-time eigenvalue-count covariances, and equal-time number variances. For a disk of mean eigenvalue count $y$, the latter obey $\mbox{Var}\mathcal N_X(D_y)=\kappa_X\sqrt y+ \beta_X/\sqrt y+o(y^{-1/2})$, with explicitly given constants for each class. Exact perturbation theory further identifies eigenvector nonorthogonality as the mechanism of short-time spectral diffusion and yields a basis-independent condition number for a two-dimensional Kramers eigenspace in class $AII^\dagger$. Direct simulations agree quantitatively with its conjectured inverse-gamma law.
item.dc:creator: Yan V Fyodorov

item.title: Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.
item.dc:creator: V. I. Gerasimenko

item.title: Phase Transitions in Learning Driven by Extremal Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.29531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study an extremal regression problem, an example of multiple instance learning (MIL), where the predictors are given as multisets, called bags. The bag elements (called instances) possess hidden labels which are pooled to produce an observed bag-level label. Max pooling is common in MIL applications, but gives rise to vanishing gradients. To handle this, modern MIL pipelines approximate the max with a softmax, treating the sharpness as a learnable parameter, denoted $\lambda$. When the max pooling model is the true data generating process, learning will be successful when $\lambda$ is increased during gradient descent, thereby driving the dynamics into regions of parameter space with vanishing gradients. To understand the conditions under which gradient descent breaks down, we study a minimal model and derive a low dimensional projection of the gradient flow in the joint limit of large bags $n$ and high dimension $d$ with $\alpha=\ln n/d$ fixed. The flow has two distinct phase transitions: an intrinsic freezing transition related to the random energy model of disordered systems, and a retrieval transition occurring in modern Hopfield networks. Numerical simulation confirms both the phase diagram and the convergence of the finite-size training gradient to its predicted asymptotic form.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Levien, Trevor GrandPre

item.title: Mechanism of delayed elastic state absorption versus fatigue failure in cyclic shear of amorphous materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study cyclic shear in a lattice elastoplastic model of amorphous materials. The model displays a threshold shear amplitude $\gamma_{\rm c}$, which increases with sample annealing. For imposed amplitudes $\gamma_0\lesssim\gamma_{\rm c}$, it shows slow progression to an absorbing elastic state. For $\gamma_0\gtrsim \gamma_{\rm c}$, it shows slow fatigue and delayed material failure. Our key contribution is to elucidate a mechanistic understanding of this behaviour. We show that progression to an absorbing state maps to single element diffusion on a finite interval with two absorbing boundaries. We derive expressions for the decay rate of the fraction of active elements, and the survival distribution. The diffusing variable is the local elemental strain, which takes two jumps stroboscopically per cycle. Once the value at any site diffuses below its yielding threshold, the element behaves elastically. This leads to a gradual accumulation of strains just below threshold. For $\gamma_0\lesssim \gamma_{\rm c}$ this diffusive behaviour is preceded by many cycles in which cooperativity between elements via stress propagation is also important. For $\gamma_0 > \gamma_{\rm c}$, stress propagation dominates and precipitates failure. For $\gamma_0\gtrsim \gamma_{\rm c}$, the same accumulation of elements just below local threshold that led to an elastic state for $\gamma_0\lesssim\gamma_{\rm c}$ accounts for the fatigue that brings the system to the brink of failure. We evidence this via simulations in which the strain amplitude artificially exceeds $\gamma_0 $ in each half cycle, before reverting to the system's actual state at $\pm\gamma_0$ and resuming the next half cycle. During fatigue, the stress-strain slope $d\sigma/d\gamma$ evolves towards unity at $|\gamma|=\gamma_0^-$, signifying perfect elasticity within cycle, yet towards zero at $|\gamma|=\gamma_0^+$, precipitating failure.
item.dc:creator: Samuel B. Walker, Suzanne M. Fielding

item.title: Closing of density wake in concentrated colloidal suspensions: two regimes governed by compressibility, friction, and self-propulsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.29801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When an obstacle moves through a compressible medium, it creates a density perturbation. Theoretical arguments regarding the shape of this density wake in Brownian suspensions either suppose infinite dilution or describe only the far field. Here, we study via experiments and numerical simulations the closing of the density perturbation just behind a circular obstacle in dense 2D suspensions of particles that are thermal or self-propelled. In the thermal case, we show that the characteristic length of the wake is a non-monotonic function of density, decreasing then increasing. We rationalise the scalings of both regimes by analytical arguments that highlight the role of the compressibility factor of the suspension. Based on this new understanding of the passive case, we show that the influence of self-propulsion observed in experiments and simulations can be understood as if the obstacle is effectively larger in an active bath, with non-trivial and distinct roles of the self-propulsion velocity and of the persistence time.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Duprez, Gianmarco Spera, Benjamin Buhl, Fran\c{c}ois Graner, Vincent D\'emery, C\'ecile Cottin-Bizonne, H\'el\`ene Delano\"e-Ayari, Mathieu Leocmach

item.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.29998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $\beta\to\beta-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.
item.dc:creator: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori

item.title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.30062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.
item.dc:creator: Atharva Naik, Madhumita Saha, David A. Huse, Manas Kulkarni, Abhishek Dhar

item.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.30118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. We address these questions in a teacher-student model with a convolutional teacher acting on $P$ input positions with correlation $c$ between positions. We compare convolutional and locally connected students trained by online stochastic gradient descent, and derive ordinary differential equations that describe their dynamics exactly in the limit of large feature dimension $D$. For uncorrelated positions ($c = 0$), the two students follow the same learning trajectory, with the convolutional student learning exactly $P$ times faster. We also find that locality affects the sample complexity: a student that matches the kernel size of the teacher recovers it from $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D)$ samples, whereas $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D\log(D))$ samples are needed with a larger kernel. For $c > 0$, spatial correlations can reduce the advantage of weight sharing. The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with $c$, whereas that of the locally connected student is independent of $c$ and overall lower when evaluated at the same learning rate. When the learning rate is instead tuned to the training horizon, however, the locally connected student wins at early times and the convolutional student at late times, with a transition that we predict analytically.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Mori, Melanie Weber

item.title: Level 2.5 large deviations and uncertainty relations for non-Markov self-interacting dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.07943v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address the general problem of formulating the dynamical large deviations of non-Markovian systems in a closed form. Specifically, we consider a broad class of ``self-interacting'' jump processes whose dynamics depends on the past through a functional of a state-dependent empirical observable. Exploiting a natural separation of timescales, \newnewtext{and under the corresponding mixing conditions,} we obtain the exact (so-called ``level 2.5'') large deviation joint statistics of the empirical measure over configurations and of the empirical flux of transitions. As an application of this general framework, we derive explicit general bounds on the fluctuations of trajectory observables, generalising to the non-Markovian case both thermodynamic and kinetic uncertainty relations. We illustrate our theory with simple examples, and discuss potential applications of these results.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Coghi, Amarjit Budhiraja, Juan P. Garrahan

item.title: Finite-time Polytropic Steering Reveals Non-monotonic Irreversibility
item.description: arXiv:2602.13765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How irreversibility evolves from slow to fast driving is a central question in nonequilibrium thermodynamics. While near-equilibrium theory predicts increasing irreversibility with driving speed, the corresponding crossover far from equilibrium is not generally resolved within a unified control framework. Here we introduce polytropic steering, in which a prescribed relation between the ensemble energy and a time-dependent control parameter continuously organizes finite-time processes between isothermal and adiabatic limits. A Fokker-Planck formulation makes the construction applicable to general confining potentials, and yields closed-form thermodynamic expressions for a harmonic trap. We find a non-monotonic irreversibility: the entropy generation decreases in both the quasistatic and fast-driving limits and exhibits a maximum at an intermediate protocol duration. The resulting most-irreversible timescale quantifies the competition between thermal relaxation and external driving. We verify the persistence of this behavior in an anharmonic optical-lattice potential and demonstrate how the same steering principle controls power-efficiency trade-offs in finite-time Brownian engines.
item.dc:creator: Cong Fu, Youhui Lin, Shanhe Su, Yu-Han Ma

item.title: Enhanced synchronization with proportional coupling in Kuramoto oscillator networks under a fixed coupling budget
item.description: arXiv:2603.29648v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an explicit coupling scheme for enhancing the synchronization of Kuramoto oscillator networks under a fixed coupling budget. We show that by scaling the interaction strength between oscillators according to their frequency detuning, synchronization is enhanced. The coupling scheme produces a crossover from a smooth Kuramoto onset to an abrupt, hysteretic synchronization transition as a single allocation parameter is varied. Our work offers a general route to efficient synchronization in engineered Kuramoto networks and provides insight into their critical behavior.
item.dc:creator: Amit Pando, Eran Bernstein, Tomer Hacohen, Nathan Vigne, Hui Cao, Oren Raz, Asher Friesem, Nir Davidson

item.title: Spectral theory for dynamical large deviations in non-Markov self-interacting processes
item.description: arXiv:2609.40329v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a spectral theory for dynamical large deviations in non-Markov jump processes and non-Markov chains, whose dynamics depends on the past through state- and jump-dependent empirical observables. We demonstrate that a multiscale Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin-Jeffreys (WKBJ) Ansatz separates fast configurational relaxation from slow memory evolution, reducing the Feynman--Kac equation for occupation and flux statistics to an eigenvalue problem for a new tilted operator coupled to Hamilton--Jacobi characteristics. This provides a computationally efficient framework for quantifying fluctuations in a broad class of non-Markovian systems. We illustrate our general results with a bistable self-induced East model.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Coghi, Juan P. Garrahan

item.title: Poisson-shot-noise induced escape dynamics of a passive particle and a dimer
item.description: arXiv:2610.26316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mean First Passage Time (MFPT) is a crucial quantity that characterizes stochastic processes in various stochastic dynamical systems across different disciplines. The inverse of the MFPT, known as the escape rate, is helpful in the context of Brownian motion and chemical processes. The MFPT dynamics of a passive particle in the presence of active noises presents a fascinating avenue. In this work, we study the dynamics of two different systems: first, a single Brownian particle and second, a dimer (two Brownian particles connected by a spring). In both cases, the systems are kept in contact with a thermal bath and an active bath, and are trapped in a bistable potential. The active bath produces kicks that follow the Poisson distribution. The MFPT of the particle and the dimer is investigated in various scenarios. Analytical results are presented for the small kick variance approximation only. In this approximation, we formulate the MFPT in two scaling regimes: a weak-noise regime characterized by classical Arrhenius scaling for escape rate and a strong-noise regime in which the MFPT scales as a power law in the effective noise strength. For the general case, the problem is solved numerically. Next, under the same approximation, the MFPT of a dimer in the small-bond-strength regime is studied using a sequential-hopping mechanism, and in the large-bond-strength regime, the MFPT is formulated using the adiabatic elimination approach. Motivated by recent studies on speeding up the escape mechanism, the MFPT of the particle and the dimer in the presence of an intermediate barrier is also examined. We deduced from the numerical results that the MFPT can be enhanced and further optimized by selecting a suitable intermediate potential profile.
item.dc:creator: Gemeit Goel, Rahul Marathe

item.title: Distinct weak antisymmetric interactions shape human brain functions as probability fluxes
item.description: arXiv:2508.20961v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The functional computation of the human brain is hypothesized to arise from the collective behaviour of the underlying neural network. A method based on an idea from equilibrium statistical mechanics has been applied to infer the underlying interaction network among the brain regions from whole-brain imaging, but recent studies have challenged the equilibrium assumption. Without equilibrium, how does the human brain encode its function in biased state transitions? Here we show that the probability fluxes, which quantify the irreversibility of state transitions, exhibit unique, task-dependent patterns in spontaneous and task-induced whole-cerebral-cortex activity. We then fit an Ising model with asymmetric interactions and reveal that the symmetric interactions among the brain regions are strong and task-independent, whereas the antisymmetric interactions are weak and task-dependent, and that the fitted model reproduces the observed fluxes for most tasks. Our results indicate that the human brain performs its functional computation by subtly modifying the antisymmetric part of the interactions among the brain regions, offering a new explanation for how a similar interaction network supports diverse brain functions. The method can be applied to the time-series data of other high-dimensional many-body systems to reveal the probability fluxes and infer the underlying interactions among components.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Horiike, Shin Fujishiro

item.title: Universal Statistics of Measurement-Induced Entanglement in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
item.description: arXiv:2512.13809v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the statistics of measurement-induced entanglement (MIE) after partial measurement on a class of one-dimensional quantum critical states described by Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids at low energies. Using a replica trick to average over measurement outcomes in the charge basis and tools from conformal field theory (CFT), we derive closed-form expressions for the cumulants of MIE. We show that exact Born-averaging over microscopic measurement outcomes becomes equivalent at low energy to averaging over conformal boundary conditions weighted by their corresponding partition functions. Our results yield distinctive critical behavior across all cumulants in the regime where the unmeasured parts of the system are maximally separated. We also obtain the full distribution of MIE, finding that it is generically bimodal and exhibits fat-tails. We corroborate our analytical predictions by numerical calculations and find good agreement between them.
item.dc:creator: Kabir Khanna, Romain Vasseur

item.title: Tunable shear thickening in active frictional non-Brownian suspensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.09620v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study tunable shear thickening in active suspensions of non-Brownian, repulsive, frictional grains using particle-based simulation, finding that activity augments the rheology beyond the friction- mediated shear thickening paradigm. Specifically, up to a crossover activity strength, increasing particle self-propulsion drives a viscosity-reducing `dethickening' of the system at large stresses, where the material would otherwise be in a thickened, highly viscous state. Above this crossover activity strength, the system enters a thickening regime. Self-propulsion introduces additional isotropic dynamics to the particles, which compete with the flow-driven formation of frictional contacts. The degree of dethickening can thus be tuned by varying a suitably-defined dimensionless active stress that quantifies this competition. Recognising the parallels between self-propulsion and other contemporary routes to dethickening, we demonstrate that our data, within the dethickening regime, are consistent with a recently proposed universal scaling framework, offering a route to tuning the rheology of dense suspensions. Moreover, using the obtained scaling relation, we infer how the shear-jamming and shear-thickening regimes can be tuned by choosing an appropriate self-propulsion strength, and partially validate these inferences with targeted simulations.
item.dc:creator: Bhanu Prasad Bhowmik, Christopher Ness

item.title: Edge universality in Floquet sideband spectra
item.description: arXiv:2604.05244v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A monochromatic voltage drive redistributes noninteracting fermions over sidebands with Bessel amplitudes. A sharp Fermi step gives the discrete Bessel source kernel, whose large amplitude edge has the Airy limit known from random matrices and propagating fronts. At zero temperature and for energy independent transmission, the deficit of the dc bias derivative of low frequency partition noise from its large bias slope is proportional to the kernel diagonal, with ac amplitude fixed. Shifting the integer threshold coordinate down by half a sideband removes the leading finite amplitude correction. For reservoirs at a common temperature, we derive the rescaled deficit's crossover through one thermal convolution per reservoir. Its leading low temperature correction is twice that of the rescaled source occupation. We specify the geometry and mode resolution needed to distinguish this signature from the full Airy point process.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: Mixed-State Topology in One-Dimensional Open Floquet Systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.25248v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the non-equilibrium topology of the steady state of a periodically driven, dissipative Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain using the ensemble geometric phase (EGP) $\phi_{\mathrm{EGP}}$, a generalisation of the Zak phase to mixed states. The coupling to thermal reservoirs is treated microscopically within Floquet-Born-Markov theory without the rotating-wave approximation. We classify the steady state rather than the generator of the dynamics, using its purity spectrum as the analogue of a band structure. We show that, within the EGP framework, the $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ structure of isolated chiral-symmetric Floquet SSH systems generally does not carry over to the steady state. Instead, the steady state carries a single invariant whose type is set by an underlying symmetry. When this symmetry holds, the invariant is $\mathbb{Z}_2$-valued, with quantised $\phi_{\mathrm{EGP}}=\pm\pi/2$ at all times and finite temperatures. The EGP can switch within a driving period, tracking the presence of edge modes in the open-boundary purity spectrum and thereby establishing a bulk-boundary correspondence. The fraction of each period spent in the nontrivial regime varies continuously with the driving frequency, and the switching disappears if the dependence of the dissipator on the drive is neglected. When the symmetry is broken, $\phi_{\mathrm{EGP}}$ is no longer quantised, but its winding over a drive period $T$ defines an invariant $\nu_T \in \mathbb Z$, with no purity-spectrum bulk-boundary correspondence. We propose that its changes signal temperature- and frequency-driven topological phase transitions. Our formalism extends to general quadratic fermionic systems with linear bath couplings.
item.dc:creator: G\"orkem D. Dinc, Alexander Schnell, Andy M. Martin

item.title: Entropy functional theory for inhomogeneous fluids
item.description: arXiv:2606.28240v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an exact variational scheme for the physics of inhomogeneous classical fluids in thermal equilibrium. A joint metadensity minimization principle is proven for the one-body density and the global interparticle distance distribution. The theory bypasses the inhomogeneous two-body density and thus remains computationally simple. A universal excess entropy functional accounts for all many-body correlations in arbitrary pairwise interacting systems. The framework is relevant for neural functional machine learning, for soft matter design, and for predicting hyperobservables, structural correlation functions, and first-principles mechanisms of entropy-energy competition.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Schmidt

item.title: Entropy functional universality: Correlation, response, many-body interaction, multi-component, quantum, hyperfunctional, and Ornstein-Zernike structure
item.description: arXiv:2607.03032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a comprehensive account of the recent entropy functional theory for the equilibrium statistical mechanics of classical many-body systems (arXiv:2606.28240). The approach is formally exact and based on a joint grand potential minimization principle for the one-body density and the global pair distance distribution. These variational fields depend respectively on position and on scalar distance, which retains the low computational complexity of standard density functional theory. Correlation effects are contained in a unique excess entropy functional, which is universal across all systems with pairwise interparticle potentials. Functional differentiation yields entropic direct correlation functionals that generate entropic response and fluctuation correlation functions via coupled Ornstein-Zernike equations. Two alternative proofs are given for the existence and uniqueness of the underlying metadensity functional map, based on generalizations of either Levy's constrained search method or Mermin-Evans proof by contradiction. Simple excess entropy approximations yield the standard mean-field and second-virial excess free energy density functionals. We describe exact entropic functional line integrals, make connections to the recent one-body fluctuation profiles, and generalize the entropy approach beyond pairwise interparticle potentials via parametric dependence or reduction operators. We also lay out the formulation for multi-component systems, the hyperfunctional for general observables, and the quantum entropy functional.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Schmidt

item.title: Microscopic study of topological phase transitions: Percolation point of view
item.description: arXiv:2607.26707v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate microscopic mechanisms underlying decoherence-induced transitions between topologically ordered states. As a first case study, we analyze the color code using topological entanglement negativity (TEN) and a disorder parameter associated with 1-form symmetry. We interpret these quantities as first- and zeroth-dimensional simplicial homological objects, respectively, and show that the transition can be understood in terms of decoherence percolation. To resolve its local structure, we introduce quasi-local TEN (QLTEN), which visualizes the spatial distribution of local topological properties and the growth of decohered regions. We further introduce explosive percolation (EP), corresponding here to biased decoherence that suppresses the formation of large decohered clusters. As a second case study, we consider the toric code on a triangular lattice under external-field-type decoherence. Numerical results show that QLTEN faithfully captures the emergence of Higgs regions and the survival of logical qubits. Although global TEN, QLTEN clusters, and string operators are strongly correlated in both models, the color code and toric code respond differently to EP patterns. This difference indicates that a universal microscopic description of decoherence-induced topological phase transitions remains challenging even for closely related systems.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Kataoka, Ikuo Ichinose

item.title: Exact quantum circuits for a lattice Boltzmann realization of the Dirac equation
item.description: arXiv:2608.06570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum lattice Boltzmann scheme of Succi and Dellar advances a four-component Dirac spinor on a lattice by a fixed sequence of local, exactly norm-preserving operations: a basis rotation, a collision, a streaming shift, and the inverse rotation. While this correspondence has been noted qualitatively, it has remained unclear whether it can be realized exactly and unitarily as a gate-model quantum circuit. This unitarity is a structural property of the scheme, which should, in principle, enable an operator-by-operator port onto quantum hardware. We give a gate-level construction of every operation of the three-dimensional Dirac QLB scheme: the fixed rotation gates, the collision gate, the streaming shift as a controlled increment on a position register, the position-dependent potential as a phase oracle, and periodic and reflecting boundary conditions as unitary circuits. Together, these constructions provide the first complete demonstration that the scheme is exactly representable in the gate model without any approximation beyond the classical method itself. We then compose them into single-axis, two- and three-dimensional time steps. On a state-vector emulator the resulting circuits reproduce the classical QLB solver to machine precision, thus verifying our quantum implementation. Our aim is representability and correctness rather than computational speedup; questions of state preparation, asymptotic cost, and hardware noise are identified as open avenues for future work. Appendices restore physical units, derive the scheme's Zitterbewegung in closed form and compare it with a trapped-ion simulation, and execute a reduced two-site instance on a Rigetti superconducting processor, where choosing the qubits from the live calibration lowers the state-preparation error. All operators, circuits, and figures are reproducible from the open-source quantumKineticMethods library.
item.dc:creator: Nilesh Sawant, Ethan Young, Kevin Patrick Griffin, Michael Martin

item.title: Discrete semiclassical theory of quantum-thermal escape
item.description: arXiv:2609.21625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dissipationless quantum-thermal escape rate from a metastable well is often written as a Boltzmann average of the Hill-Wheeler flux over a continuum of energies. This continuum treatment diverges exponentially at low temperature, because it pairs the quantum partition function of the well with a classical flux integral. Retaining the discrete nature of the quasibound spectrum removes the divergence exactly, and the resulting rate is obtained in closed form on both sides of the crossover temperature $T_0$. Evaluating a uniform Kemble transmission probability on Bohr-Sommerfeld levels further removes the parabolic-barrier error and recovers the WKB decay rate of the lowest resonance at zero temperature. Benchmarked against the resonances of cubic and quintic potentials, obtained by complex scaling, this uniform semiclassical rate stays within $9\%$ of the exact one over eleven orders of magnitude. Below $T_0$, the rate rises above its zero-temperature plateau with the level spacing as activation energy, and the plateau ends at a temperature $T_1$ noticeably below $T_0$. In an isolated well, whose levels are not replenished, the thermal rate is only the initial slope of a decay which ceases to be single exponential at $T_1$, while at $T_0$ the initial escape moves from tunneling inside the well to the barrier top. We discuss implications for Josephson junctions, single-electron pumps, and nuclear burning in dense stellar matter.
item.dc:creator: Luca Salasnich, Cesare Vianello

item.title: Observation of Universal Quantum Chaos at Shallow Depths
item.description: arXiv:2609.28623v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Universal statistical laws are a hallmark of quantum chaos. A natural route to probing them in quantum circuits is offered by the statistics of output probabilities, which for sufficiently deep chaotic circuits approach the Porter--Thomas distribution. Here we show, theoretically and experimentally, that the approach to this limit is itself universal, and is organized into geometry-dependent universality classes. At shallow depths, growing only logarithmically with system size, we derive universal output-probability distributions that differ markedly from Porter--Thomas statistics, and we test them on a programmable superconducting processor. Two-dimensional lattices, open one-dimensional chains, and periodic rings exhibit distinct universal forms, retaining signatures of geometry and boundary topology within the same logarithmic-depth regime. Within each class, the distributions depend on only two parameters: an effective many-body Thouless scale and the accumulated number of incoherent errors. Extracting these directly from measured bitstring frequencies provides access to scrambling, entanglement growth of the target state, and global fidelity, without reconstructing or classically simulating the implemented circuit. We also identify a noise-driven transition between output statistics retaining system-wide quantum correlations and those reproducible by independent small patches. Our results establish universality beyond Porter--Thomas statistics as a quantitative tool for characterizing noisy quantum processors.
item.dc:creator: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Hugo L\'oio, Thomas J. Maldonado, Shashwat Kumar, Pedram Roushan, Andrea De Luca, Jacopo De Nardis

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. The two mean-square quantities are linearly comparable. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length, and the result extends to nonnegative observation weights with nonnegative Fourier transform. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2610.27179v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems. We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variants for quasipotential calculations, and neural network techniques. The Schl\"{o}gl model of chemical bistability serves as a running example, illustrating both scalar and spatially extended settings. Appendices provide self-contained background on stochastic calculus and Markov jump processes.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Cirigliano, William D. Pi\~{n}eros, Anna Poggialini, Grant M. Rotskoff, Eric Vanden-Eijnden
